bounds.domain: One live native capture, one explicit draft request, one stale queued user reservation, one automatic reopen and one subsequent explicit live start. The original capture starts running or can finish opening after cancellation.
bounds.scope: The existing controller worker serializes native startup, full capture-resource retirement, draft acquisition and explicit draft finalization before live acquisition. Cancellation fences immediately. Failed source-close acknowledgement retains the original owner and refuses replacements. A cancelled stale user reservation cannot clear the automatic-reopen fence.
bounds.assumptions: A successful physical close actually releases its source. Host epoch, protected-surface, permission and call-focus checks reflect their real state at each bridge admission check. The admitted draft finalizer throws when cleanup is unconfirmed. The controlled JVM harness runs production controller, admission, capture and resource classes; Android bridge wiring is compiled and checked separately.
bounds.limitations: No AudioRecord or MediaRecorder hardware runs in this model or JVM harness. It does not establish device microphone availability, permission-dialog correctness, AudioFocus behavior, provider delivery, PCM/VAD quality, Android callback transport, arbitrary callers or process-death recovery. A failed physical release fences this controller until process replacement; no retry or time bound is promised. Progress depends on native startup, stop, release and the Java worker settling. No silent timeout permits a new owner.
bounds.progress: Under weak fairness of original startup, stop, successful physical release and the serial drain continuation, an admitted handoff returns a draft acknowledgement or refusal. Release failure can instead cause an explicit refusal. Without fairness a native operation can block forever.

assumptions: Weak fairness of original native startup, stop, release and drain continuation. No physical-device progress or time bound is established.
